newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seen shaky after three pct drop.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seen shaky after three pct drop.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - JUNE 2 --------------
+ IPE Brent may extend its sideways consolidation on Monday but it was still seen in a precarious position after a three percent drop during last week's four sessions, chartists said.
+ July Brent's technical floor was put at last week's low of $19.09 and then a gap at $18.88 to $18.80 from early May.
+ Gas oil, also pausing, may hold $171.75, a double bottom.
IPE Brent crude futures were expected to trade sideways on Monday, extending the consolidation from late last week after prices fell three percent to end the month of May, chartists said.

The sharp drop since the July contract peaked at $20.60 in mid-May and then gapped lower last Tuesday, however, will likely reassert itself and force prices toward a downside gap at $18.88 to $18.80, they warned.
"The intraday perspective is flat above $19," said Wee Woon Whai, technical analyst at Standard and Poor's MMS International in Singapore.
She cited neutral trend indicators such as stochastics and a moving average convergence-divergence (MACD).
"At this point there is no sign that it is going higher but because it has fallen so much it looks consolidative," she said. "Unless it can close above $20, the general trend is still down."
She said $20 was a psychological as well as a previous congestive resistance level. On the downside, a break below $19 could translate into a quick drop to $18.50, she said.
July Brent closed on Friday at $19.40 after ending the previous week at exactly $20.
On the spot continuation chart, last week's low of $19.09 was the weakest since May 12, when prices left another gap at $19 to $18.94.
"We believe the market will consolidate for the next couple of days," said Wong Hui Ming, desk manager at CA Global Futures. "The trading range on July Brent should be about $19.87 to $18.87."
He believed the commodity funds were still long the market and as long as prices held above his 63-day moving average, now crossing at $18.81, it would support prices.
"We don't believe the market will have a sharp drop of another 50 cents," he said. "If it tests $19.09 to $19 it will be a good buying opportunity."
June gas oil looks equally strong while it holds above its 63-day moving average at $168, he said. He put resistance at $176.75, based on trendline and Fibonacci analysis.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8185
